title: Diagonal root invariants and the nonnegative exponent lattice
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge1$ an integer invertible in $A$, $\zeta\in A^\times$ satisfy $\zeta^n=1$ and $1-\zeta^a\in A^\times$ for $1\le a<n$, and $r\ge0$. Choose $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$ and a subgroup $H\subseteq(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$. Put
$$B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),\qquad P=\mathbf N^r.$$
Let $H$ fix $A$ and send $x_i$ to $\zeta^{h_i}x_i$. Define
$$L=\{a/n\in(1/n)\mathbf Z^r:\ \textstyle\sum_i h_i a_i=0\pmod n\text{ for all }h\in H\},\qquad Q=L\cap(1/n)\mathbf N^r.$$
Then $Q$ is a fine saturated sharp monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $Q^{\rm gp}=L$, and the inclusion $P\hookrightarrow Q$ is injective with $nQ\subseteq P$. Its group cokernel $L/\mathbf Z^r$ is finite and annihilated by $n$. Here sharp means that the only additive unit is $0$. Give $A$ its $\mathbf Z[P]$-algebra structure by $z^{e_i}\mapsto t_i$, where for any additive monoid $S$, $\mathbf Z[S]$ is free as an abelian group on $z^s$, with $z^sz^{s'}=z^{s+s'}$. There is an $A$-algebra isomorphism
$$A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }B^H,\qquad a\otimes z^q\longmapsto a\prod_i x_i^{nq_i}.$$
It takes $1\otimes z^{e_i}$ to $t_i$. In particular, if $c_q$ denotes the image of $1\otimes z^q$, then $c_q^n=\prod_i t_i^{nq_i}$. This includes $r=0$ and $n=1$ and imposes no regularity or domain assumption on $A$.

source.place: Ancestor lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve proof Step 3, uniformization input, through the present item: ILO Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, equality of the parameter-root invariant ring with the monoid base change; Expose VI 2.2--2.3, printed pp.72--73, standard Kummer charts and their diagonal characters. The rational-lattice convention makes the inclusion P into Q literal.

proof.text: The congruence conditions defining $L$ are kernels of additive homomorphisms $(1/n)\mathbf Z^r\to\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, so $L$ is a subgroup and contains $\mathbf Z^r$. Consequently $P\subseteq Q$, its inclusion is injective, and $nq\in P$ for every $q\in Q$. The map $L/\mathbf Z^r\to(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$ sending the class of $a/n$ to $a\bmod n$ is well defined and injective: equality of residues is precisely that the difference lies in $\mathbf Z^r$. The target is a finite set, and multiplying any class by $n$ gives zero. Thus the group cokernel has the asserted finiteness and exponent.

source.place: IX, Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133: the intermediate lattice and the Kummer inclusion; explicit coordinate verification.

proof.text: Let $S=\{b\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^r:b/n\in L\}$. Coordinatewise division gives every $q\in Q$ a unique expression $q=m+b/n$, with $m\in P$ and $b\in S$: write $nq_i=nm_i+b_i$, and use $\mathbf Z^r\subseteq L$ to see $b/n\in L$. Hence $Q$ is generated by the finite set $\{e_1,\ldots,e_r\}\cup\{b/n:b\in S\}$. Its embedding in the abelian group $L$ makes it integral. Every $l\in L$ is a difference of elements of $Q$, since one can choose $m\in\mathbf N^r$ so that $l+m$ is coordinatewise nonnegative and write $l=(l+m)-m$. The group completion is therefore $L$ (equality of two differences is equality of cross sums in this embedded monoid). If $kl\in Q$ for $k>0$ and $l\in L$, each coordinate of $l$ is nonnegative, so $l\in Q$. Finally $q,-q\in Q$ forces $q=0$. These check exactly fineness, saturation, group completion and sharpness; only the monoid definitions of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] are used, with no log-scheme hypothesis.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69 (fs terminology), and IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133; explicit residue-box argument for this orthant monoid.

proof.text: If $A$ is the zero ring, then $B$ and $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ are zero rings, and their unique map is the required isomorphism; all monoid claims were proved independently in Steps 1--2. For the remaining steps assume $A\ne0$. Put $B_j=A[x_1,\ldots,x_j]/(x_i^n-t_i:1\le i\le j)$ and $B_0=A$. The polynomial evaluation property of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and the quotient description of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] identify $B_{j+1}$ with $B_j[T]/(T^n-t_{j+1})$: send old generators to themselves and $T$ to $x_{j+1}$ in both directions; the relations vanish, and the composites fix coefficients and every generator. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], the latter quotient has $B_j$-basis $1,T,\ldots,T^{n-1}$. Induction now gives the $A$-basis $x^b=\prod_i x_i^{b_i}$, $b\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^r$, of $B$. Indeed, expand each coefficient in the old basis for spanning; for uniqueness, collect by the last exponent, use the new power-basis independence, and then the old independence. The induction starts with $1$ in $A$; it also shows $B_j\ne0$, so the displayed monic polynomial has degree $n$ at each application.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, parameter-root quotient; power-basis argument supplied explicitly using Stacks Tag 04GG (algebra-lemma-characterize-henselian) as recorded in the cited leaf.

proof.text: For $h\in H$, scaling $x_i$ by $\zeta^{h_i}$ preserves $x_i^n=t_i$, because $\zeta^n=1$; scaling by $-h$ is its inverse, and adding $h$ corresponds to composing scalings. Thus this is the specified action by $A$-algebra automorphisms, independent of residue representatives. For $f=\sum_b a_bx^b$, Step 3 gives $h(f)=f$ exactly when $(\zeta^{\sum_i h_i b_i}-1)a_b=0$ for every $b$. If $b\notin S$, choose $h\in H$ with $\sum_i h_i b_i\not\equiv0\pmod n$. Its representative $c$ satisfies $1\le c<n$, so $1-\zeta^c$ is a unit and $a_b=0$. If $b\in S$, every such character is $1$ and $x^b$ is fixed. Therefore the fixed subring $B^H=\{f\in B:h(f)=f\text{ for all }h\in H\}$ has $A$-basis $(x^b)_{b\in S}$. No averaging or exactness theorem for invariants is used.

source.place: VI 2.3, equation (2.a), printed pp.72--73, and IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133; coefficientwise diagonal-character calculation.

proof.text: Set $R=\mathbf Z[P]$. By Step 2, addition defines a bijection $P\times S\to Q$, $(m,b)\mapsto m+b/n$. As monoid rings have the abelian-group bases given in the statement, every element of $\mathbf Z[Q]$ has a unique finite expression $\sum_{b\in S}f_bz^{b/n}$ with $f_b\in R$: collect the integer coefficients of $z^{m+b/n}$ for each $b$, and use uniqueness of $(m,b)$ for independence. Thus $\mathbf Z[Q]$ is a free $R$-module with basis $(z^{b/n})_{b\in S}$. This does not assert that $S$ is closed under addition, nor that $Q$ is a product of monoids.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, monoid base change; explicit expansion in the residue-box representatives of Step 2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free] with $R=\mathbf Z[P]$, its map to $A$ specified in the statement, and the free module $\mathbf Z[Q]$ of Step 5. It gives the $A$-basis $u_b=1\otimes z^{b/n}$, $b\in S$, of $C=A\otimes_R\mathbf Z[Q]$. Define $\psi:\mathbf Z[Q]\to B$ by $z^q\mapsto x^{nq}$. Exponents add and $z^0$ maps to $1$, so extension by finite sums is a ring map. For $q\in Q$ its image is fixed, since its character on $h$ is $\zeta^{\sum_i h_i(nq_i)}=1$. For $m\in P$, $\psi(z^m)=x^{nm}=\prod_i t_i^{m_i}$, which is the image of $z^m$ under $R\to A\to B^H$. Thus $\psi$ and the structure map $A\to B^H$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras (the latter via $R\to A$), with $R$-algebra structure on $\mathbf Z[Q]$ from $P\subseteq Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (1), $C=A\otimes_R\mathbf Z[Q]$, the tensor product of $R$-modules of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], is a commutative ring with $(a\otimes f)(a'\otimes g)=aa'\otimes fg$ and unit $1\otimes1$, and an $A$-algebra through $a\mapsto a\otimes1$; this is the algebra structure meant in the statement. By its clause (2), applied to $A\to B^H$ and $\psi$, there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\Phi:C\to B^H$ with $\Phi(a\otimes f)=a\psi(f)$, in particular $a\otimes z^q\mapsto ax^{nq}$. Since $\Phi(a\otimes1)=a$, it is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133, monoid-base-change identification; Stacks Tag 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product) for the balanced construction and Module.Basis.baseChange for the basis.

proof.text: The map $\Phi$ sends $u_b$ to $x^b$ for every $b\in S$. These are the bases of Steps 6 and 4 with the same index set. Explicitly its inverse as an $A$-linear map sends $\sum_{b\in S}a_bx^b$ to $\sum_{b\in S}a_bu_b$; uniqueness of both coefficient expansions makes the two composites identities. Consequently the unital multiplicative $A$-linear map $\Phi$ is an $A$-algebra isomorphism, with exactly the formula in the statement. In $C$, the balancing relation gives $1\otimes z^{e_i}=t_i\otimes1$, and its image is $x_i^n=t_i$. For any $q\in Q$, $nq\in P$, so $c_q^n=\Phi(1\otimes z^{nq})=\prod_i t_i^{nq_i}$. This also proves the same power identity for $1\otimes z^q$ in $C$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133: explicit inverse and the parameter compatibility of the monoid base change.

proof.text: When $r=0$, all lattices and monoids are zero, $H$ is trivial and $S$ has the single empty tuple; both algebras and the map above are $A$ and its identity. When $n=1$, $H$ is trivial, $L=\mathbf Z^r$, $Q=P$, and $S=\{0\}$; the quotient relations give $x_i=t_i$ and both algebras again identify with $A$. Zero or zero-divisor parameters cause no change to the power-basis induction or to the coefficient cancellation, which cancels only the units $1-\zeta^c$ in $A$. Thus no regularity, reducedness or domain assumption was introduced.
